note: 2026-09-03, the day's first and only batch, chairman-authorised, and IT IS A DELIBERATE CHANGE OF AIM THAT I OWN AND DISCLOSE HERE RATHER THAN IN THE RECORD ALONE. The 2026-09-02 close-out's next step 1 specified a G3 docket-geometry batch against ICSID ARB/12/1 (Tethyan Copper v Pakistan). I AM NOT FIRING IT. That same close-out's escalation 6 put the question to the operator in terms I adopt: eight consecutive sessions of instrument and method work, and 'on the research question the day returned nothing.' The docket carrying that work is a mineral-exploration dispute; it does not reach this council's theme (IP as a covered investment; a regulatory or judicial measure as the challenged conduct; a live jurisdictional or admissibility doctrine) and no amount of further character geometry on it will make it reach the theme. This repository mentions ARB/12/1 451 times and the three ON-THEME seed dockets 88 (ARB/16/34), 75 (ARB/10/7) and 70 (UNCT/14/2) times combined-per-docket; that ratio is the finding. The prior chairman recorded its own continuity decision as taken 'because continuity is the chairman's default, not because I think the case for it is strong.' I read that as an invitation to today's chair and I am taking it. THIS BATCH POINTS AT THE THEME. Rows 1-6 are the three seed dockets' ICSID case-detail pages, each probed for 'Status of Proceeding' (the page-state anchor for that URL, read first for that URL, graded by sha256) and 'Published Decisions' (the right edge, where a post-award annulment, revision, rectification or enforcement development would surface). A live post-award development on ANY of the three would be an actual thematic finding, which eight days of ARB/12/1 geometry structurally could not produce. ROW 7 IS A SINGLE CONTINUITY ANCHOR ON ARB/12/1 - 'Status of Proceeding' only - so that docket's page state stays observed and tomorrow can resume the G3 geometry at full strength if the operator rules that way; ONE row is not a resumption of the geometry programme and no seat may read it as one. Row 8 is the example.com tail control. EIGHT REQUESTED ROWS AGAINST MAX_URLS OF 12 - FOUR FREE - plus the relay's own prepended head control = NINE RECORDS; MAX_URLS caps requested rows only, per scripts/fetch_relay.py lines 195-199, which truncate targets to MAX_URLS and only then prepend fetch_one(CONTROL_URL). NOTHING IN THIS BATCH IS PRE-REGISTERED AS A FORECAST. No seat has read today's state of any of these four pages, no prior offset or reach figure from any earlier record applies to them, and there is no sha256 of record for the three seed dockets at all. Every row here is a PROBE. A returned excerpt establishes what its own 400 characters contain and nothing about what lies outside them; an absent literal establishes that excerpt_of found no match on the returned body, WHICH IS A STATEMENT ABOUT THE FETCH, NOT ABOUT THE DOCKET, and may not be reported as 'no published decisions' or 'no development.' The three seed dockets' case numbers are taken from this repository's own record (ARB/16/34 Bridgestone Licensing Services v Panama; ARB/10/7 Philip Morris v Uruguay; UNCT/14/2 Eli Lilly v Canada), not from memory and not from a search; the relay is not a discovery channel (METHODOLOGY Part VIII) and every URL here is a page this record already identifies. If a case-detail URL returns 404 or a non-200, THAT IS INFORMATION ABOUT THE URL PATTERN FOR THAT CASE NUMBER and is to be reported as such, never as information about the case. TODAY'S RECORD MUST CITE THIS BATCH'S REDUCTION BY COMMIT SHA AND BLOB SHA, NEVER BY PATH: the relay's overwrite defect is structural, fires on every council merge by construction, and the file at this path will be rewritten by the merge of the very record that reads it.
